title: Threat Hunting with Wireshark: Network Forensics

stages.title: Stage 1

lessons.title: Course Introduction
lessons.objective: Build anticipation by introducing the course, the real investigation problems it

lessons.title: What You Will Be Able to Investigate
lessons.objective: Walk through the eight case files and connect each deliverable to a SOC task: triage, scoping, hypothesis testing, escalation or reporting.

lessons.title: Threat Hunting, Monitoring and Incident Response
lessons.objective: Distinguish proactive hunting from alert investigation and response; explain when an unanswered question should become a structured hunt.

lessons.title: Read the Network Story Before Naming the Attack
lessons.objective: Use a short capture to identify who talked to whom, when and over which protocols before assigning an attack label.

lessons.title: What a Packet Can and Cannot Prove
lessons.objective: Separate observable network events from assumptions about process execution, user intent, credential theft and successful compromise.

lessons.title: How the Practical Investigations Work
lessons.objective: Introduce case briefs, progressive hints, evidence worksheets and solution walkthroughs; show how to record a reproducible answer.

lessons.title: Your Starting Skills Check
lessons.objective: Assess TCP/IP, DNS, HTTP, TLS and basic Wireshark navigation through a diagnostic capture, then assign targeted refresher material.

stages.title: Stage 2 — Build a Reliable and Isolated Analysis Lab

lessons.title: Choose the Minimum Practical Lab
lessons.objective: Set up an analysis workstation with Wireshark and TShark; explain why all required investigations can run from supplied offline captures.

lessons.title: Install and Verify the Analysis Tools
lessons.objective: Verify capture permissions, available interfaces and tool versions on the chosen operating system; record the environment used for demonstrations.

lessons.title: Create Your Threat Hunting Profile
lessons.objective: Configure useful columns, absolute timestamps, coloring rules and saved filters so another analyst can reproduce the same view.

lessons.title: Understand Where the Capture Comes From
lessons.objective: Compare endpoint, TAP, SPAN, gateway and cloud capture perspectives; show how NAT, routing and missing east-west traffic affect attribution.

lessons.title: Collect Controlled Traffic Safely
lessons.objective: Capture traffic only from the approved lab segment; use a bounded collection window and explain ring-buffer retention and capture-filter tradeoffs.

lessons.title: Troubleshoot the Lab Before You Hunt
lessons.objective: Resolve empty captures, interface selection, timestamp display and misleading name resolution; save a clean baseline profile and checklist.

stages.title: Stage 3 — Evidence Quality, Capture Limits and Preservation

lessons.title: Inspect the Capture Before the Payload
lessons.objective: Review file format, size, duration, encapsulation and available interface metadata with Wireshark and capinfos.

lessons.title: Preserve Originals and Work on Copies
lessons.objective: Create a case directory, record a SHA-256 hash and preserve the original; explain why an edited or sanitized copy needs its own identity.

lessons.title: Check Truncation, Drops and Missing Directions
lessons.objective: Recognize short snapshot lengths, capture loss, asymmetric collection and incomplete streams; document how each changes confidence.

lessons.title: Make Time Comparable Across Sources
lessons.objective: Normalize displayed times to UTC, retain original time-zone information and distinguish measured clock offsets from guessed corrections.

lessons.title: Handle Sensitive Packet Content
lessons.objective: Identify credentials, personal data and embedded secrets in captures; apply access controls and use redacted derivatives for teaching or sharing.

lessons.title: Write an Evidence Intake Note
lessons.objective: Complete a concise acquisition and handling record covering origin, scope, file hash, transformations, analyst and known blind spots.

stages.title: Stage 4 — Turn a Suspicion into a Testable Hunt

lessons.title: Start with a Question Worth Answering
lessons.objective: Turn a vague concern such as unusual outbound traffic into a hypothesis with a population, time range and observable behaviour.

lessons.title: Choose Hypothesis, Baseline or Intelligence Entry Points
lessons.objective: Compare the three starting approaches and decide when an indicator should trigger broader behavioural investigation.

lessons.title: Map Behaviour to ATT&CK Carefully
lessons.objective: Use ATT&CK to organize investigation questions; distinguish a plausible technique mapping from evidence that the technique actually occurred.

lessons.title: Define the Pivots and Stop Conditions
lessons.objective: Plan host, time, protocol and peer pivots; define what would support, weaken or leave the hypothesis unresolved.

lessons.title: Project 1: The Unexpected Outbound Connection
lessons.objective: Investigate a synthetic office capture containing scheduled software activity and a suspicious external session; explain the competing explanations.

lessons.title: Debrief the Hunt and Set the Next Action
lessons.objective: Present an evidence-backed disposition, identify the next useful data source and record a reusable hunt question rather than only an IP address.

stages.title: Stage 5 — Build Precise Filters and Useful Analyst Views

lessons.title: Capture Filters and Display Filters Solve Different Problems
lessons.objective: Compare collection-time filtering with analysis-time filtering, including why a display filter cannot recover traffic excluded at capture time.

lessons.title: Compose Filters with Clear Boolean Logic
lessons.objective: Combine address, protocol, port and time conditions with explicit parentheses; test the difference between matching one endpoint and both directions.

lessons.title: Work with Fields, Strings and Repeated Values
lessons.objective: Use field existence, comparisons, contains and supported regular expressions; inspect repeated fields and validate expressions against known packets.

lessons.title: Add Columns That Answer the Hunt Question
lessons.objective: Build columns for stream identifiers, DNS names and relevant application fields; explain missing values and protocol-dependent availability.

lessons.title: Color, Comment and Bookmark the Evidence
lessons.objective: Use coloring rules and packet comments consistently while keeping annotations separate from conclusions that still need corroboration.

lessons.title: Test a Filter Against Positive and Negative Examples
lessons.objective: Build a small filter notebook containing intent, expression, expected matches, benign counterexample and known limitations.

stages.title: Stage 6 — Read TCP, UDP and Reassembled Conversations

lessons.title: Read TCP Setup, Transfer and Teardown
lessons.objective: Follow SYN, acknowledgments, sequence numbers and connection closure to establish whether a session was attempted, established or interrupted.

lessons.title: Interpret Retransmissions and Expert Information
lessons.objective: Investigate loss, out-of-order delivery, duplicate acknowledgments and resets; avoid treating Wireshark diagnostic flags as intrusion verdicts.

lessons.title: Follow Streams Without Losing Context
lessons.objective: Use Follow Stream and stream filters to reconstruct visible content, then return to packet timing, direction and the original capture.

lessons.title: Understand Reassembly and Decode As
lessons.objective: Investigate segmented application messages and nonstandard ports; use Decode As only when the evidence supports the protocol choice.

lessons.title: Investigate UDP and ICMP Conversations
lessons.objective: Analyze request-response patterns, unsolicited traffic and ICMP errors while accounting for the absence of TCP-style session state.

lessons.title: Recognize Fragmentation and Offload Artifacts
lessons.objective: Compare fragmented traffic, checksum offload symptoms and incomplete reassembly; state when packet capture conditions prevent reliable interpretation.

stages.title: Stage 7 — Baseline Hosts, Services and Traffic Patterns

lessons.title: Establish the Environment and Asset Roles
lessons.objective: Use the supplied inventory to distinguish workstations, resolvers, servers and network devices before evaluating unusual communication.

lessons.title: Use Protocol Hierarchy for First-Pass Triage
lessons.objective: Summarize protocol composition and identify unexpected protocols without assuming a small or unfamiliar category is hostile.

lessons.title: Pivot Through Endpoints and Conversations
lessons.objective: Rank peers by volume, duration and fan-out; distinguish frame bytes, payload size and unique application data.

lessons.title: Build Time-Based Views with I/O Graphs
lessons.objective: Compare bursts, periodic exchanges and quiet periods using consistent intervals; explain how aggregation can hide short events.

lessons.title: Compare Like-for-Like Baselines
lessons.objective: Account for business hours, backups, updates, role differences and collection windows when comparing hosts or days.

lessons.title: Prioritize Anomalies with a Decision Log
lessons.objective: Rank candidate sessions using rarity, asset sensitivity, temporal context and corroboration; retain a reason for dismissing benign outliers.

stages.title: Stage 8 — Scale Packet Triage with TShark and Capture Utilities

lessons.title: Translate a GUI Filter into TShark
lessons.objective: Read a capture with -r, apply a display filter with -Y and compare the selected frames with the Wireshark GUI.

lessons.title: Export Fields for a Timeline
lessons.objective: Use -T fields, explicit -e fields and controlled delimiters; handle absent and repeated values before importing the output into a spreadsheet.

lessons.title: Summarize Endpoints and Conversations in Batches
lessons.objective: Apply consistent offline commands to several known input files and record tool version, profile, filter and source hash.

lessons.title: Split, Merge and Inspect Captures
lessons.objective: Use editcap, mergecap and capinfos on working copies; preserve originals and explain renumbering, duplicate packets and timestamp ordering.

lessons.title: Project 2: Build a Repeatable Triage Pack
lessons.objective: Process a multi-file case into endpoint summaries, a filtered evidence set and a timeline that another analyst can reproduce.

lessons.title: Verify the Automation Against the Packets
lessons.objective: Spot-check output rows in Wireshark, investigate mismatched counts and document where an automated summary loses necessary context.

stages.title: Stage 9 — Investigate DNS Behaviour and Suspicious Resolution

lessons.title: Follow a Complete DNS Transaction
lessons.objective: Connect queries, responses, answer records and client-resolver relationships; distinguish a recursive resolver from the original requesting endpoint.

lessons.title: Analyze Failures, Bursts and Repeated Lookups
lessons.objective: Compare NXDOMAIN activity, retries and repeated names with application errors, misconfiguration and potential malicious behaviour.

lessons.title: Investigate Unusual Names and Record Types
lessons.objective: Examine long labels, many unique subdomains and TXT responses as clues; explain why none independently proves a tunnel or malware.

lessons.title: Pivot from a Name to Subsequent Connections
lessons.objective: Connect DNS answers to later sessions using timing and address history; account for shared hosting, multiple answers and stale caches.

lessons.title: Handle Missing DNS and Encrypted Resolution
lessons.objective: Explain cache hits, hardcoded addresses, DoH and DoT visibility limits; identify resolver or endpoint logs that could fill the gap.

lessons.title: Triage a Suspicious DNS Case
lessons.objective: Compare noisy legitimate service discovery, a failing application and a suspicious query sequence; document which pattern deserves deeper analysis.

stages.title: Stage 10 — Reconstruct Web Delivery and Initial Access Clues

lessons.title: Read HTTP Requests and Responses as a Sequence
lessons.objective: Connect methods, status codes, hosts, paths and redirects to reconstruct a user or application interaction.

lessons.title: Investigate Redirects and Download Chains
lessons.objective: Follow a synthetic lure through multiple destinations; separate observed delivery from assumptions about how the user reached the first page.

lessons.title: Inspect Headers, Forms and Content Types
lessons.objective: Review visible user agents, content types and request bodies, comparing their declared purpose with the actual captured exchange.

lessons.title: Export Visible Objects for Safe Examination
lessons.objective: Export a supplied inert object, calculate its hash and record source frames; explain why exporting content is different from executing it.

lessons.title: Project 3: The Suspicious Download
lessons.objective: Reconstruct a staged download case using a PCAP and supplied endpoint event excerpt; decide whether the evidence supports delivery, execution or both.

lessons.title: Explain What HTTPS Hides
lessons.objective: Repeat the investigation on an encrypted version and identify which conclusions remain possible from metadata and which require other evidence.

stages.title: Stage 11 — Recognize Scanning, Discovery and Network Anomalies

lessons.title: Investigate Port and Host Fan-Out
lessons.objective: Compare one-host-many-ports and many-hosts-one-port patterns using connection attempts, responses and timing.

lessons.title: Analyze Failed and Partial Connections
lessons.objective: Use SYN, reset and ICMP patterns to identify attempted reachability without equating every failure with scanning.

lessons.title: Examine ARP, DHCP and Local Discovery
lessons.objective: Review address resolution, lease context and unexpected local discovery activity; explain what one observation point can reliably see.

lessons.title: Investigate Name-Resolution Anomalies
lessons.objective: Analyze supplied LLMNR, NBNS and DNS examples for unexpected responders; distinguish suspicious response behaviour from proof of credential capture.

lessons.title: Compare Authorized Scanners and Adversarial Discovery
lessons.objective: Use inventory and maintenance windows to contrast vulnerability scanning, administration and unexplained internal reconnaissance.

lessons.title: Build a Discovery Scope Map
lessons.objective: Summarize the initiating hosts, attempted targets, observed responses and gaps in coverage; request endpoint context for the initiating process.

stages.title: Stage 12 — Investigate Authentication and Credential-Related Signals

lessons.title: Recognize Common Authentication Conversations
lessons.objective: Identify visible Kerberos, NTLM-related and LDAP exchanges and connect them to normal domain activity using a supplied environment map.

lessons.title: Distinguish Failures, Retries and Suspicious Bursts
lessons.objective: Compare authentication errors and repeated connections with password changes, stale services and suspicious login activity.

lessons.title: Inspect Cleartext Exposure in Training Traffic
lessons.objective: Locate synthetic credentials in deliberately insecure sample protocols; document exposure and remediation without using the credentials.

lessons.title: Understand Ticket and Relay Investigation Limits
lessons.objective: Discuss network clues associated with suspicious ticket requests or relay-like paths, then identify the host and identity logs required for confirmation.

lessons.title: Project 4: Discovery Followed by Authentication Activity
lessons.objective: Combine a discovery capture, authentication traffic and sanitized identity logs to test whether a service fault or intrusion better explains the sequence.

lessons.title: Write a Credential-Risk Escalation
lessons.objective: Report affected assets, observable exchanges, unresolved account questions and a prioritized request for supporting evidence.

stages.title: Stage 13 — Find and Validate Beacon-Like Behaviour

lessons.title: Define a Beaconing Hypothesis
lessons.objective: Specify what recurring contact would look like in the available capture and distinguish periodicity from confirmed command-and-control activity.

lessons.title: Measure Inter-Arrival Timing
lessons.objective: Extract comparable connection or request start times and calculate intervals; avoid mixing packets within a session with separate check-ins.

lessons.title: Interpret Jitter, Gaps and Long-Lived Sessions
lessons.objective: Compare regular, variable and interrupted patterns while accounting for capture duration, network loss and application scheduling.

lessons.title: Compare Direction, Size and Session Reuse
lessons.objective: Review request-response asymmetry, duration and recurring peers as supporting clues; avoid universal thresholds detached from the environment.

lessons.title: Rule Out Updates, Monitoring and Keepalives
lessons.objective: Test the same analysis against known benign periodic traffic and use asset role and endpoint ownership to explain matches.

lessons.title: Document a Beacon Candidate
lessons.objective: Produce a ranked candidate with the measured pattern, benign alternatives, confidence level and next evidence request.

stages.title: Stage 14 — Investigate TLS, QUIC and Visibility Limits

lessons.title: Read the Visible TLS Handshake
lessons.objective: Inspect available handshake information and distinguish fields visible in the capture from data protected by the negotiated protocol.

lessons.title: Use Server Names and Certificates Carefully
lessons.objective: Evaluate visible SNI and certificate information where present; account for shared infrastructure, TLS version and encrypted handshake elements.

lessons.title: Decrypt a Controlled TLS Session
lessons.objective: Load the supplied matching session secrets into Wireshark and verify decryption against a known lab exchange; keep secrets with restricted case materials.

lessons.title: Troubleshoot Decryption Expectations
lessons.objective: Explain why an arbitrary server private key cannot generally decrypt modern forward-secret sessions and why missing secrets or packets may block analysis.

lessons.title: Recognize HTTP/2, QUIC and HTTP/3 Boundaries
lessons.objective: Identify transport and application clues, note connection multiplexing and explain how available keys and dissector support change visibility.

lessons.title: Hunt When Names and Payloads Are Hidden
lessons.objective: Compare destination, timing and flow context while recognizing ECH and encrypted DNS limitations; formulate a targeted endpoint or proxy evidence request.

stages.title: Stage 15 — Investigate DNS Tunneling and Alternative Channels

lessons.title: Define the Channel and the Observable Claim
lessons.objective: Distinguish command exchange, connectivity checks and potential data transfer; state which claim the available evidence can actually test.

lessons.title: Analyze Query Shape, Diversity and Volume
lessons.objective: Measure label lengths, unique names, record types and response patterns; compare results with telemetry and content-delivery traffic.

lessons.title: Use Timing and Direction to Strengthen the Case
lessons.objective: Correlate repeated DNS exchanges with host activity and estimate observed data-bearing content without equating wire bytes to stolen data.

lessons.title: Examine Synthetic Encoded Training Content
lessons.objective: Inspect supplied harmless encoded markers and explain the difference between encoding and encryption; record what the controlled example proves.

lessons.title: Review ICMP and Unusual-Port Candidates
lessons.objective: Examine supplied ICMP payload patterns and application traffic on unexpected ports; consider diagnostics and protocol misclassification as alternatives.

lessons.title: Build a Channel Investigation Worksheet
lessons.objective: Combine structural, temporal and contextual evidence and state whether the outcome is suspicious, explained or unresolved.

stages.title: Stage 16 — Correlate a Multi-Protocol Command-and-Control Case

lessons.title: Start from a Weak Indicator and Expand Carefully
lessons.objective: Pivot from a single candidate destination to related sessions while preserving time scope and avoiding unbounded association.

lessons.title: Build a Host-to-Infrastructure Timeline
lessons.objective: Connect resolution, outbound sessions and changes in destinations; account for NAT and shared services when attributing activity.

lessons.title: Evaluate Fingerprints and Infrastructure Similarity
lessons.objective: Treat available client or server fingerprints and certificate reuse as leads; discuss collisions, legitimate software reuse and tool-dependent availability.

lessons.title: Project 5: The Quiet Callback
lessons.objective: Investigate a synthetic endpoint with periodic TLS traffic, DNS changes and benign background activity using PCAPs and a supplied process-network log.

lessons.title: Challenge Your Own C2 Conclusion
lessons.objective: Review conflicting evidence, missing process context and a legitimate agent lookalike; revise confidence rather than forcing a binary answer.

lessons.title: Deliver a C2 Investigation Brief
lessons.objective: Present observed behaviour, supporting host evidence, confidence, scope and a proposed containment decision for the response owner.

stages.title: Stage 17 — Investigate SMB and Windows East-West Activity

lessons.title: Establish Normal Windows Network Relationships
lessons.objective: Use role and share information to distinguish ordinary workstation access, administration and unexpected workstation-to-workstation traffic.

lessons.title: Read SMB Sessions and Visible Operations
lessons.objective: Follow session setup, tree connections and file activity when decoded and visible; account for encrypted SMB payloads.

lessons.title: Analyze Administrative Shares and File Transfers
lessons.objective: Investigate unusual share access and transferred training artifacts while distinguishing file copy from confirmed remote execution.

lessons.title: Correlate RPC and Service-Related Traffic
lessons.objective: Connect visible RPC-related exchanges to internal sessions and explain why endpoint service or process records are needed to confirm execution.

lessons.title: Track Internal Fan-Out and Sequencing
lessons.objective: Identify an expanding set of internal peers and compare its timing with normal software deployment and backup activity.

lessons.title: Write a Lateral-Movement Hypothesis
lessons.objective: Document the source, targets, operations, time window and host evidence needed to confirm or refute movement between systems.

stages.title: Stage 18 — Investigate Remote Services Across Platforms

lessons.title: Recognize Remote-Service Session Patterns
lessons.objective: Identify RDP, SSH and WinRM-related connections from decoded traffic and supplied context; avoid relying only on default ports.

lessons.title: Understand Encrypted Remote-Access Limits
lessons.objective: Explain why an encrypted RDP or SSH session does not reveal the commands executed, the authenticated user or whether access was authorized.

lessons.title: Correlate Remote Access with Identity Events
lessons.objective: Join network sessions to sanitized authentication and asset records using time, address mapping and known collection limitations.

lessons.title: Investigate Pivoting and Multi-Hop Sequences
lessons.objective: Reconstruct a plausible chain across internal hosts while distinguishing temporal correlation from proof of a single operator.

lessons.title: Project 6: The Internal Hop
lessons.objective: Investigate a workstation-to-server sequence containing SMB and remote-service traffic; compare it with a documented administrator session.

lessons.title: Scope the Response Without Overreaching
lessons.objective: Identify affected and potentially affected systems, unresolved identity questions and targeted follow-up collection requests.

stages.title: Stage 19 — Detect and Quantify Potential Data Exfiltration

lessons.title: Define What Data Loss Would Mean in the Case
lessons.objective: Identify the asset, destination, channel, data sensitivity and authorization context needed to assess an outbound transfer.

lessons.title: Analyze Upload Patterns and Directionality
lessons.objective: Compare visible HTTP uploads, file-transfer protocols and encrypted sessions using initiator, payload direction and time context.

lessons.title: Look for Low-Volume and Staged Transfers
lessons.objective: Evaluate repeated small transfers, off-hours activity and visible staging clues while distinguishing a long capture window from stronger evidence.

lessons.title: Measure Bytes Without Double Counting
lessons.objective: Separate frame bytes, TCP payload and unique application content; account for retransmissions, overhead and incomplete captures.

lessons.title: Distinguish Backup, Synchronization and Exfiltration
lessons.objective: Use supplied business context to test legitimate storage, cloud synchronization and administrative-transfer explanations.

lessons.title: State the Data-Loss Confidence Level
lessons.objective: Report visible content, estimated transfer volume and unknowns separately; request DLP, proxy, storage or endpoint evidence where needed.

stages.title: Stage 20 — Reconstruct a Multi-Stage Network Intrusion

lessons.title: Build a Consistent Case Time Window
lessons.objective: Reconcile capture coverage, clock differences and asset mappings before joining multiple stages of activity.

lessons.title: Connect Entry, Callback and Internal Activity
lessons.objective: Use shared hosts, timing and supporting logs to connect observations without assuming every nearby event belongs to the same intrusion.

lessons.title: Trace Collection and Outbound Transfer Clues
lessons.objective: Relate visible internal access to later external traffic and identify the additional evidence needed to establish the data involved.

lessons.title: Project 7: From Suspicious Download to Outbound Transfer
lessons.objective: Investigate a synthetic incident containing a delivery chain, callback, internal access and possible exfiltration alongside realistic benign noise.

lessons.title: Handle a Misleading Lead and Missing Evidence
lessons.objective: Assess an injected red herring and a capture gap; explain whether each changes the incident scope or only the confidence level.

lessons.title: Present the Incident Narrative
lessons.objective: Deliver a concise chronological account with evidence references, alternative hypotheses and prioritized next actions.

stages.title: Stage 21 — Use Packet Evidence in Incident Response

lessons.title: Fit Hunting into the Response Process
lessons.objective: Connect a hunt to triage, analysis, containment, recovery and improvement while situating response within broader risk-management preparation.

lessons.title: Write a High-Value Escalation
lessons.objective: Summarize observed behaviour, impacted assets, confidence, urgency and the next decision the incident lead needs to make.

lessons.title: Choose the Next Evidence Collection
lessons.objective: Prioritize endpoint, identity, DNS, proxy, firewall or flow records based on a specific unanswered question and retention risk.

lessons.title: Recommend Containment with Operational Context
lessons.objective: Compare host isolation, credential action and network controls as proposed response choices; document evidence preservation and service impact considerations.

lessons.title: Verify Containment and Look for Recurrence
lessons.objective: Use an agreed post-action observation window to test whether suspicious communication recurs while acknowledging unmonitored paths.

lessons.title: Project the Lessons into Recovery and Improvement
lessons.objective: Record root-cause uncertainties, visibility gaps and follow-up owners; avoid declaring eradication from a quiet packet capture alone.

stages.title: Stage 22 — Build a Defensible Network Forensics Report

lessons.title: Create a Unified Evidence Timeline
lessons.objective: Join packet and log observations using source identifiers and normalized time while retaining original timestamps and uncertainty.

lessons.title: Separate Facts, Inferences and Unknowns
lessons.objective: Label every major claim and identify the minimum corroboration needed to raise or lower confidence.

lessons.title: Make Packet Citations Reproducible
lessons.objective: Reference original file hash, frame number, timestamp and stream context; explain why exported or merged captures have different frame numbers.

lessons.title: Write the Technical Investigation Narrative
lessons.objective: Describe method, findings, scope, affected assets and limitations in an order that lets a reviewer reproduce the reasoning.

lessons.title: Write the Executive Summary
lessons.objective: Translate the same findings into business impact, confidence, immediate decisions and next actions without unsupported attribution.

lessons.title: Peer-Review the Case and Fix Weak Claims
lessons.objective: Use a supplied checklist to detect missing evidence, inconsistent times, overclaimed data loss and vague recommendations.

stages.title: Stage 23 — Turn Hunts into Reusable Detections

lessons.title: Choose the Durable Behaviour to Monitor
lessons.objective: Separate short-lived indicators from recurring behaviour and identify which telemetry can observe the proposed detection.

lessons.title: Write a Reusable Hunt Playbook
lessons.objective: Document hypothesis, scope, required fields, packet-analysis steps, decision points, known false positives and escalation criteria.

lessons.title: Translate Packet Findings into Detection Logic
lessons.objective: Express a candidate rule as clear pseudocode for an appropriate log or flow source; avoid treating a Wireshark filter as a complete production detection.

lessons.title: Test Against Benign and Suspicious Cases
lessons.objective: Evaluate the proposal against labelled course captures and logs; record missed cases, false positives and coverage limitations.

lessons.title: Tune Thresholds to the Environment
lessons.objective: Use a supplied baseline and operational context to adjust thresholds; document what the small training dataset cannot establish about production performance.

lessons.title: Plan Ownership, Monitoring and Review
lessons.objective: Assign a detection owner, deployment validation steps and review cadence; turn the investigation's blind spots into a visibility improvement backlog.

stages.title: Stage 24 — Capstone: Lead a Complete Threat Hunt

lessons.title: Receive the Capstone Case Brief
lessons.objective: Review business context, available captures, asset inventory and rules of engagement; define the first hypothesis without solution hints.

lessons.title: Plan the Investigation and Preserve the Evidence
lessons.objective: Create the evidence register, select relevant time windows and identify collection gaps before narrowing the traffic.

lessons.title: Project 8: Investigate the Unfamiliar Incident
lessons.objective: Work through an unseen synthetic case involving suspicious outbound activity, internal access and possible data loss with several benign lookalikes.

lessons.title: Defend the Findings Under Review
lessons.objective: Respond to challenges about attribution, encrypted visibility, missing traffic and the distinction between compromise and suspicious behaviour.

lessons.title: Compare with the Annotated Solution
lessons.objective: Review the instructor's evidence chain and acceptable alternative conclusions; explain where a cautious inconclusive result earns full reasoning credit.

lessons.title: Complete Your Portfolio and Next-Step Plan
lessons.objective: Package a sanitized report, evidence index, hunt playbook and detection proposal; identify the skills and telemetry needed for further practice.
